newsitem.title: FRANCE: NATO summit could take place on May 27 - France.
newsitem.headline: NATO summit could take place on May 27 - France.

text.p: France said on Wednesday a Paris summit for Russia to sign a partnership document with NATO could take place on May 27 if differences with Moscow on the alliance's enlargement eastwards were resolved.
"This summit will take place on May 27 in Paris if there is an accord," a Foreign Ministry spokesman told a news briefing, adding that talks were continuing.
NATO Secretary General Javier Solana, who failed to reach a breakthrough in talks with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on Tuesday, was due in Paris later in the day.
French officials said he was to have separate meetings with Prime Minister Alain Juppe and Foreign Minister Herve de Charette in the evening.

Primakov proposed the Paris summit during a visit to the French capital last week. The Kremlin indicated after Solana's talks that a planned pact on future relations was far from ready, and President Boris Yeltsin has made clear that Moscow would not sign the document just for the sake of sticking to the target date.

The main sticking point is Russia's fear that the alliance's plans to invite in former Soviet-bloc countries in July will lead to a military build-up near its borders. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are the front-runners to join.
